jobs.title: RF Design Engineering Intern (10668) at Qorvo
jobs.description: Employer: Qorvo Expires: 09/30/2026 Qorvo’s Internship Program is designed for college students currently enrolled in an accredited Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD program. Qorvo offers real work experience, exposure to upper management, and the opportunity to pursue full-time opportunities, as available. Qorvo’s Internship Program offers:Challenging, skill-building assignmentsMentoring and coaching from industry expertsLaunch & Learns and other learning opportunitiesCollaborative team-based work environmentNetworking and social eventsFinal presentation to business leaders Qorvo’s RF Design Engineering Internships are offered in our High Performance Analog business group. Specific projects and responsibilities will be determined based on the business needs at the time of the internship assignment. Team Overview:The Antenna Technologies team, part of the Defense Missions Technology group within Qorvo's Defense & Aerospace (D&A) business unit, develops advanced phased array antenna solutions that enable our customers to accomplish critical missions. As an intern with our team, you will collaborate with world-class antenna designers, RF engineers, and test professionals that create state-of-the-art products for Satellite Communications, Line-of-Sight Communications, Radar, and other defense and aerospace applications. Responsibilities may include:Complete intern project based on alignment between candidate capabilities and antenna team requirements. Example projects may include:Development of demonstration system that highlights existing antenna team designs that can be used at Qorvo public events and trade shows.Perform testing on existing designs that allow the antenna team to understand performance variations over production.Implement new calibration routines and validate with measured data.Validate new test setups for over the air testing of existing antennas.Support ongoing antenna team design work by performing one or more of the following tasks:Collaborate with mmWave antenna, electrical, RF component, and printed circuit board design engineers to develop mmWave phased array designs for emerging markets and applications.Design passive circuit components, including power splitters/combiners, microstrip and stripline transmission lines, and impedance transformers, using AWR, CST, or HFSS.Support hands-on testing and troubleshooting of RF and mmWave phased array antenna prototypes, including power supplies, control circuits, and RF/mmWave circuits. Qualifications:Currently enrolled in an Engineering degree program, pursuing a Master’s degree (MSEE or equivalent) or higherMinimum GPA 3.0 or higherPrior RF circuit design and/or antenna design experience using AWR, CST, and/or HFSS.Experience designing and/or testing RF and mmWave circuits, coupons, and systems.Preferred Qualifications:Experience with scripting or programming in a language such as Python.Experience designing or testing phased array antennas, beamforming networks, antenna modules, or RF front-end assemblies.Experience working with PCB fabrication and assembly vendors to support prototype builds, design reviews, and failure analysis.Hands-on experience using RF/mmWave test equipment such as VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power meters, and probe stations.Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to summarize trade studies, test results, and design decisions for cross-functional teams. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship by the Company. Competitive hourly pay commensurate with experience: $31/hr - $42/hr (subject to change dependent on physical location) Posted salary ranges are made in good faith. Qorvo reserves the right to adjust ranges depending on the experience/qualification of the selected candidate as well as external competitiveness and internal comparability. Base compensation is one element of Total Rewards offered at Qorvo. More information on the Total Rewards package can be shared upon request.

jobs.description: Employer: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency Expires: 09/30/2026 Summer 2027 College Internship - Source Career Field External HeaderSource: External Applicants OnlyOpen: 2026-08-31Closed: 2026-09-30Band: 01/02Location: St Louis, MO, Springfield, VA, Denver, CO, Las Cruces, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Patrick SFB, FLCover LetterApplicants are not required to submit a cover letter for employment consideration with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. However, a cover letter is recommended. Applicants will have the option to attach a cover letter in the Qualifications - Attachments step of the online application.Pay Band, Salary Range - Ext2026 DC Salary Chart (Step 10 Max):Band 1 $30,249 - $75,059Band 2 $57,736 - $101,0972026 St. Louis Salary Chart (Step 10 Max):Band 1 $27,108 - $67,264Band 2 $51,740 - $90,5972026 Denver Salary Chart (Step 10 Max):Band 1 $29,477 - $73,142Band 2 $56,262 - $98,515Permanent Change in StationPERMANENT CHANGE IN STATION: PCS expenses are not authorized.NGA Marketing MessageThe National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is the world leader in Geospatial Intelligence. We analyze imagery and data from many sources and incorporate it into visual displays of essential information for use in national defense, homeland security and safety of navigation. The extraordinary talents and skills of our teams of analysts and other professionals are vital to our success as the worldwide provider of GEOINT.Know the World, Show the Way...from Seabed to Space!Assignment DescriptionASSIGNMENT DESCRIPTION: College Interns perform a variety of functions and tasks in support of the organization to which they are assigned. Work assignments will involve problem identification, analysis, and resolution. Specific duties may include the preparation and presentation of briefings directly related to work assigned. They must be in attendance at and enrolled in a graduate, baccalaureate, or associate degree program. Students are placed on one-year temporary appointments, which can be extended in one-year increments until the student graduates. Their appointment terminates upon graduation or when the student no longer attends school, even if the expiration date on the current appointment has not been reached.Additional InformationADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The Source Career Field would be a good fit for you if you're majoring in Geography, Cartography, Earth Science, International Studies, Anthropology, or Linguistics. As an intern in the Source career field, you will be at the center of the GEOINT enterprise, collaborating with a diverse set of customers and providers to acquire the content, data, and information needed to address the nation’s most pressing intelligence challenges.While your specific placement will be determined by mission needs, this internship will provide you with exposure to the critical functions that enable the agency to deliver timely and relevant GEOINT. Potential areas of focus include:- Collection Strategy & Operations: Develops comprehensive multi-INT strategies, manages tasking requirements, and ensures the seamless delivery of critical GEOINT data. (Includes roles like Source Strategies Analyst, OPIR Operations Analyst, and Foundation Collection Analyst).- Navigation & Safety Analysis: Analyzes worldwide aeronautical, maritime, and bathymetric data to support the safety of global navigation and intelligence requirements. (Includes roles like Aeronautical Analyst, Maritime Analyst, and Bathymetrist).- Geodetic & Earth Sciences: Analyzes the Earth's physical properties, gravity, magnetic fields, and satellite orbits, and conducts geophysical surveys to support advanced DoD applications. (Includes Geodetic Earth Scientists, Geodetic Orbit Scientists, and Geodetic Surveyors).- Human Geography & Open Source Research: Applies expertise in socio-cultural dynamics, foreign languages, and open-source intelligence to understand regional issues and support national security goals. (Includes Human Geographers, Human Geography Linguists, Open Source Research Analysts, and Librarians).- Cartography & Photogrammetry: Performs advanced image assessment and ensures the quality, accuracy, and currency of mapping and cartographic information produced for partners worldwide. (Includes Cartographers and Photogrammetrists).Transcript Upload Instructions: All applicants must upload proof of current enrollment as part of their application. This includes your most recent unofficial transcript showing the date, university information, and GPA. Freshmen may upload a letter of enrollment from the university in place of a transcript. Experience identifying and gathering the data necessary to resolve routine problems6. Experience explaining fundamental AI concepts and/or technologies used for routine tasksEDUCATION REQUIREMENT: Incumbent must be enrolled in an associate degree program, baccalaureate, or graduate program.Special Info ExternalAs a condition of employment at NGA, persons being considered for employment must meet NGA fitness for employment standards.- U.S. Citizenship- Security Clearance - Top Secret /Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI)- Polygraph & Drug Test- Direct Deposit- Trial Period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. HD personnel will provide additional information if applicable.Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the Assignment Description, Additional Information Provided By the Selecting Official, and the Qualification Requirements; and then construct their resumes to highlight their most relevant and significant experience and education for this job opportunity. This description should include examples that detail the level and complexity of the performed work. Applicants are encouraged to provide any education or degree information referenced in the announcement that is relevant. If education is listed as a mandatory requirement, only degrees obtained from an institution accredited by an accrediting organization recognized by the Secretary, US Department of Education will be accepted. You must use the NGA resume builder and limit your resume to 2 pages.In accordance with section 9902(h) of title 5, United States Code, annuitants reemployed in the Department of Defense shall receive full annuity and salary upon appointment. They shall not be eligible for retirement contributions, participation in the Thrift Savings Plan, or a supplemental or re-determined annuity for the reemployment period. Discontinued service retirement annuitants (i.e., retired under section 8336(d)(1) or 8414(b)(1)(A) of title 5, United States Code) appointed to the Department of Defense may elect to be subject to retirement provisions of the new appointment as appropriate. (See DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 300). Reemployed annuitants must meet additional selection criteria as outlined in the DODI 1400.25, v300.All candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, disability, or sexual orientation.NGA provides reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. A performance pay process is conducted each year to determine a potential base pay salary increase and/or bonus. An employee's annual performance evaluation is a key factor in the performance pay process.This position is a DCIPS position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1601. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. Additional information concerning NGA's hiring process can be found by visiting NGA Hiring Process.All announcements close at 11:59PM EDT on the closing date listed. jobs.title: Business Development Research Intern at NatureServe
jobs.description: Employer: NatureServe Expires: 09/30/2026 Business Development ​Research Intern About NatureServeFor 50 years, NatureServe has been the authoritative source for biodiversity data throughout North America. With an international network of over 60 Natural Heritage Programs and Conservation Data Centers across the United States and Canada (“the Network”), NatureServe is the leading source of information on rare and endangered species and the ecosystems on which North American species depend. To protect threatened biodiversity, NatureServe works with over 1,000 conservation scientists to collect, aggregate, and standardize biodiversity statistics, providing comprehensive data to the public for strategic conservation efforts. NatureServe and its network programs develop and manage the most comprehensive data for over 100,000 species and ecosystems, answering fundamental questions about what the critical elements of biodiversity are, where they are found, and how they are doing. About the role​​NatureServe is seeking a Business Development Research Intern to support the growth of our biodiversity data business. You’ll work directly with the Director of Biodiversity Data Sales to research prospective companies, understand how they are organized, and identify the right decisionmakers for outreach. This is a part-time, paid internship, well suited to a graduate student or recent graduate with an interest in conservation, biodiversity, or environmental science, combined with research or business-development experience. ​The internship offers hands-one experience in business development and market research within the growing biodiversity, environmental, and geospatial data sector. You’ll gain exposure to how companies use environmental data in real-world decisions, while developing practical research skills and familiarity with the organizations, technologies, and career paths shaping this field.​On a recurring (approximately weekly) basis, you'll receive a set of target companies and guidance on the types of roles or business units we want to reach. Your research will help us understand who the right people are and how best to approach each organization. For each company, you will:​Review the company's website and public materials to understand its structure, identifying the correct business unit for large or complex organizations.​Identify 2–3 high-quality contacts per company who closely match the target roles provided, prioritizing people with direct responsibility for the relevant product, service line, or purchasing decision.​Verify each contact's current employment, title, and business unit using LinkedIn and other public sources.​Identify and verify business email addresses using verification tools, clearly flagging anything that can't be verified.​Compile findings into a shared tracker: full name, title, business unit, email, verification status, LinkedIn profile, and notes.​Flag companies where no suitable contact can be identified, rather than guessing or submitting unverified information.​Join a regular (approximately weekly) check-in to review completed lists, ask questions, and calibrate the approach as target roles evolve.​Accuracy and relevance are the priorities throughout. The goal is to minimize bounced emails and outreach to the wrong people, not to maximize volume. Contacts should be independently verified using reliable sources such as company websites, LinkedIn, and an email verification tool rather than relying on AI-generated contact information. What you'll doKey responsibilities for the Business Development Research Intern include but are not limited to:Research and identify potential corporate, government, and nonprofit partners that align with NatureServe's mission and strategic priorities Find and verify accurate contact information including names, titles, emails, and organizational structure for target leadsEnter and maintain lead and contact information in Salesforce and shared research trackersHelp segment leads by outreach priority (sector, geography, funding potential, etc.)Flag outdated or inaccurate data for correctionSupport the business development and sales team by preparing outreach lists and background materialsDig into background research on prospective partners ahead of outreach or meetingsTrack outreach activity and results to help the team report on lead generation progressProvide light administrative support on partnership tracking (e.g., updating pipeline status)Share research findings clearly with the team so they can act on itOther duties as assigned QualificationsRequired Skills & Experience:​​Strong research and information-gathering skills​Comfortable digging through LinkedIn, company websites, and public sources to find accurate contacts​High attention to detail and accuracy, especially in data entry​Strong written communication skills​Self-motivated and able to manage your own time in a remote role​Comfortable with Microsoft Office/Google Workspace; willing to learn CRM or database tools (training provided)​Interest in biodiversity, environmental data, GIS, sustainability or related fields.Preferred Certifications, Training, or Education:Current undergraduate or graduate student, or recent graduate, in environmental science. data, GIS, sustainability, business, or related field. Curiosity about how data and technology are used to solve environmental problems is strongly preferred. Physical Demands and Work EnvironmentThe physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.Work Conditions:% Time Remote: ​100%​Travel Required: ​No​On-Call Requirement: ​No​ Physical RequirementsSitting​​Typing / Computer UseRepetitive Motion Reasonable AccommodationsNatureServe is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Human Resources at [insert email/phone] to request an accommodation.The pay range for this role is $25 USD per hour (Remote)

The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments, and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries. As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people are critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and collaboration. Morgan Stanley provides an opportunity for individuals to apply their skills in a dynamic business environment through meaningful work and professional development. We foster a culture of diverse perspectives, growth and collaboration that help individuals reach their full potential. 2027 Internal Audit - Technology Audit Summer Analyst Program (New York) Summer Analysts join the Morgan Stanley Internal Audit Department in June for a comprehensive 10-week internship and development program that provides participants with exposure to various functions across Internal Audit and coverage areas within the Firm. Training Program The Summer Program includes training on internal audit fundamentals and Morgan Stanley's audit methodology, engagement with senior leadership, cross-divisional networking opportunities, peer mentorship, community service opportunities, and a group project in which Summer Analysts present what they have learned through the program to a broader audience. Participants selected for the Technology Track will also learn about cutting-edge technology, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, machine learning, algorithmic trade engines, pricing models, digital banking, advisory services, and cloud computing. Individuals who successfully complete the internship program may be considered for the Internal Audit Full-Time Analyst program following college graduation, which includes a brief rotation on the Advanced Analytics & Innovation team. This provides full-time Analysts with the opportunity to learn and apply analytics skills and leverage innovative technology (e.g., GenAI) throughout the program. Roles and Responsibilities Develop a working knowledge of business and technology principles and basic auditing standards Develop knowledge of audit tools and testing techniques Execute a wide range of assurance activities (e.g., audits, continuous monitoring, closure verification) with guidance Produce quality work in accordance with team/ department priorities and assigned deliverables (e.g., documenting narratives, executing control testing and communicating results to management) Execute testing procedures by performing test steps, gathering evidence, documenting results, and escalating issues, exceptions, or questions Contribute to messages regarding risk and business impact within relevant coverage area Collaborate with colleagues across the team Responsibilities may vary according to your coverage area. Qualifications and Skills Graduates between December 2027 and June 2028 and has less than one year of full-time professional experience Technology Audit: Pursues a bachelor’s degree (computer science, information systems or a technology-related field preferred, but not mandatory) and demonstrates working knowledge of Information Security and Technology Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 Affiliation with the Institute of Internal Auditors or the Information Systems Audit and Control Association preferred, but not mandatory Demonstrates critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills​ Communicates verbal and written messages in a clear and concise manner​ Effectively collaborates with others and adapts to a dynamic environment ​ Pays attention to detail​ and quality Seeks guidance and solicits feedback to further self-development Applicant Process and Deadline In order to be considered, candidates must apply with their resume through the Morgan Stanley website and complete their HireVue digital questionnaire. Resumes will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled or the application deadline, whichever comes first. Applications must be submitted by September 25, 2026 at 11:55 PM EST and HireVues completed by September 28, 2026 at 11:55 PM EST in order to be considered. Your noted graduation date is what is used to determine eligibility, and you must be able to join as a full-time Analyst in June 2028, if hired or offered an internship Expected base pay rate for the role will be $33.66 per hour at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs. Morgan Stanley's goal is to build and maintain a workforce that is diverse in experience and background but uniform in reflecting our standards of integrity and excellence. At Cianbro, it is believed that “no one in this room is smarter than all of us” and interns and seasoned construction experts collaborate to the benefit of the group as well as the individuals. As a result of the mentoring process, interns will expand their experience and have the opportunity to apply their knowledge to a variety of landmark projects.Career Development – After one or multiple summer internships, interns have the opportunity for their internship to lead to a full-time career opportunity, as many of Cianbro’s internships do.Technology – Interns are provided with the technology needed not only to perform their job at Cianbro but to establish technical skills and familiarity with industry-specific technology.Cianbro is committed to people, pride, and progress. jobs.description: Employer: Affiliated Engineers, Inc. Expires: 10/01/2026 Join a Team Where Engineering Excellence Drives Opportunity At Affiliated Engineers, Inc. (AEI), we bring together expertise and innovation to solve the most complex challenges. Since 1978, we’ve supported mission-driven organizations in designing systems and environments that advance society and improve lives. Today, with more than 900 professionals across 22 offices, we help shape the future of healthcare, science and technology, energy, education, and other vital sectors. From elevating patient care in Mayo Clinic’s world-class hospitals to enabling discovery in high-containment laboratories for U.S. agencies and driving environmental progress with Microsoft’s renowned Thermal Energy Center, our work enriches the human experience, safeguards the environment, and pushes the boundaries of possibility. AEI consistently earns national recognition from leading industry publications, including Building Design+Construction, Engineering News-Record, and Consulting-Specifying Engineer, with distinctions such as being named the #1 Laboratory Engineering Firm in the nation and receiving multiple Best of the Best Project awards, underscoring the lasting legacy of our work. At AEI, you’ll join a collaborative community where your expertise fuels innovation, your ideas drive progress, and your work helps shape a brighter future. As a Commissioning Engineer Intern in our Atlanta office, you will help us empower our clients to achieve energy-efficient building solutions, save global environments, and create a better, greener future for all. Why we need you:In this role, you will have the opportunity to approach engineering in unconventional ways: testing the installations rather than designing them. You will apply your knowledge while working on significant and complex projects, work alongside professionals known for advanced engineering solutions, observe how a successful engineering firm operates, establish ties that could solidify your professional future, and learn within a friendly, supportive environment. Expertise of our most successful Commissioning Engineer Intern: Enrollment in Mechanical or Architectural Engineering program from ABET accredited school.Completed 3 years of coursework or have a junior standing.Minimum GPA of 2.5.Leadership involvement in extracurricular activities/student organizations. Effective skills to help you flourish:Strong spoken and written communications skills.Detail oriented and able to follow logical flows.Excellent organization and time management skills.Quick technical comprehension and motivation focused on client outcomes.Able to effectively prioritize multiple tasks.Effective working individually and within team environments When you work here, you can expect:A flexible, collaborative environment where your well-being matters—because your best work happens when you’re supported.Real opportunities to grow—through mentorship, professional development programs, and exposure to high-impact projects across disciplines.To collaborate with inspiring teammates who challenge the status quo, foster innovation, and pave the way for future leaders.A benefits package that offers health, dental, vision, and retirement, a performance-based year-end bonus, and thoughtful perks tailored to your needs—whether that's a flexible work environment, wellness resources, or community-focused initiatives, we’ll continue to invest in. If this dynamic environment and the chance to contribute to transformative projects resonate with your ambitions, we would love to connect with you. Join us and make an impact!Apply online at https://aeieng.com/about/careers/If you know someone who would thrive in this role, please share this posting with them directly via email or through your LinkedIn network.AEI is proud to be an EEO/AA Employer/Vet/Disabled.

jobs.title: Industrial Design - PAID Summer Internship / Job (focus on Woodshop) at Camp Winadu
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Winadu Expires: 10/01/2026 Spend your summer in the beautiful Berkshire Mountains! We are seeking a skilled individual to join our team. This is an Industrial Design Internship with a focus on Woodworking and as the Woodshop Director at camp, you will be responsible for teaching groups of campers in our wood shop. You will work with and teach campers how to cut wood using various saws, drills, stencils, tools, and equipment and help them make projects such as baseball bats, model cars, skateboards, and more. You will also manage the inventory of all shop supplies, submit supply requests for items needed, and maintain the upkeep and safety of the shop.Students or recent graduates looking to add to their portfolio are welcome to apply.In addition to running the Woodshop, you will be a camp counselor taking part and guiding campers through daily camp activities, special events and serving as a role model. Staff live at camp and reside in a cabin alongside their group of campers. This is a seasonal, paid position from mid-June to mid-August. Food, housing, a travel stipend, comprehensive staff training, and days off are included as part of the compensation package.Working at Winadu is an awesome opportunity to gain hands-on experience, all while making a difference in the life of a child and have a ton of fun doing it! To learn more about the value of working at camp for your career, visit www.winadujobs.com

jobs.title: Safety Intern at Interstates
jobs.description: Employer: Interstates Expires: 10/02/2026 Help Build a Safer Future—Starting with Your CareerAt Interstates, safety is more than a checklist—it is how we care for our people, serve our clients, and pursue a better way to work.As a Safety Intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience in construction and manufacturing safety while working alongside experienced Safety Managers, Safety Technicians, supervisors, and craft professionals. it may be obtained during the internship.Previous construction or manufacturing experience is helpful but not required. We’re looking for students who are curious, dependable, collaborative, and committed to helping others work safely.Travel: Approximately 80–90%; interns are typically assigned to one U.S. location for the summerOpportunities: National Construction and ManufacturingWhy Intern at Interstates?At Interstates, you’ll be treated as a team member—not just an intern. You’ll receive:Mentorship from experienced safety professionalsCareer coaching and professional developmentHands-on experience on real projectsOpportunities in national construction and manufacturingPer diem and travel pay, as applicableCompany discount programTeam celebrations and community outreach opportunitiesPotential opportunities to continue your career with Interstates after graduationA Safety Culture with Proven ResultsInterstates is committed to a Zero Injury culture, where every employee plays a role in creating a safe workplace. Our safety performance has earned recognition including ABC National Safety Excellence Awards, ABC STEP Diamond Awards, CURT Construction Industry Safety Excellence Awards, and NSC Safest Companies with Distinction awards.In 2024, Interstates reported an EMR of 0.54, TRIR of 0.79, and DART of 0.37—results made possible by the daily commitment of our field leaders, craft professionals, safety teams, and support staff.Ready to turn your classroom knowledge into real-world experience and help build safer workplaces across the country? Apply for the Interstates Safety Internship today.

jobs.description: Employer: CAGE Civil Engineering Expires: 10/02/2026 Title: Civil Engineer Intern - Summer 2027 Description CAGE Engineering is a respected leader in civil engineering, land surveying, and construction management, known for delivering practical, high-quality solutions tailored to each client's needs. Our land development work spans residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional projects. Our team is committed to excellence and integrity, and we offer a collaborative, supportive environment where team members can grow. Join us and become part of a company that values expertise, invests in its people, and drives projects that shape communities for the better. Position Overview As a Civil Engineer Intern with CAGE, you will join a design team working on real client projects from day one, no busy work. You will develop technical skills in Civil 3D and site design, and build professional skills like networking and organization, through a series of hands-on trainings, and you will check in regularly with a mentor throughout the summer. You will also have office hours, time set aside each week for interns to meet one-on-one with CAGE leaders, ask questions, and get to know the people leading the company. Success in this role looks like steady growth in your technical skills, real contributions to your project team, and a strong sense of what a career at CAGE could look like. Typically Reports To: Project Engineer Typical Years of Experience: In current pursuit of a BS in Engineering; no prior professional experience required Key Responsibilities Design and draft land development plans using AutoCAD Civil 3D Support the production of design documents and calculations, including code and ordinance research, site planning, and stormwater management calculations Help prepare preliminary and final construction documents, stormwater pollution prevention plans, and permit documents Prepare site, grading, and utility plans that illustrate site developability based on learned constraints Participate in meetings with internal and external clients to review concept plans and discuss project direction Attend site visits to gather data used in design Attend project team meetings to discuss timelines, budgets, and design constraints Take part in CAGE's trainings on both technical and professional development topics Meet regularly with your assigned mentor and attend office hours, dedicated time each week to meet one-on-one with CAGE leaders Necessary Qualifications In current pursuit of a BS in Engineering from an accredited university Familiarity with CAD Focused, motivated, and results oriented Strong desire to learn and advance one's technical skills Ability to learn quickly and accept constructive criticism Team-oriented with strong communication skills Why CAGE? At CAGE, we excel as problem solvers, prioritize cost-conscious design, and deliver real value to our clients. We build strong relationships founded on trust and follow-through, and we look for people who share our enthusiasm and work ethic. Our interns get more than a summer job. You will get hands-on technical trainings led by our own engineers, non-technical trainings covering professional skills like networking and organization, a mentor who checks in with you regularly throughout the summer, and office hours, dedicated time each week to sit down one-on-one with CAGE leaders, all while working on real projects that matter to our clients. jobs.title: (#REF951M) 2027 Structural Engineer Summer Internship - Seniors and MS Students at KPFF Consulting Engineers
jobs.description: Employer: KPFF Consulting Engineers - Los Angeles Structural Expires: 10/02/2026 KPFF is seeking summer interns interested in experiencing the daily life of a Structural Engineer. We provide you with a summer packed with training programs to prepare you to be successful, activities to help you connect with our team, and real-world projects to apply your skills. At KPFF, 2 out of 3 of our interns return as full-time employees or return for another internship in the next year. Who We Are Looking For Students curious about Structural Engineering and wanting to understand the daily life of a Structural Engineer. We enjoy working with interns who are eager to contribute to their teams and who are interested in making connections and getting to know the people they work with. For this role you will need to have completed a bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering (with an emphasis in Structures or Architectural Engineering, prior to the start of the internship.You are interested in Structural Engineering and would like the opportunity to be exposed to a wide range of projects and conditions. You enjoy working with and learning from others to create work that you are proud of. You take the initiative to solve challenging problems and are a proactive team member.What You Will Be DoingAs a Structural Engineering Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in structural design, working closely with our experienced engineers on real-world projects. You will have the opportunity to apply your academic knowledge, develop your skills, meet other students who are in the same eld, and contribute to meaningful work. You will assist in the preparation of calculations and construction documents on active jobs under the guidance of project leaders. You will have the opportunity to participate in project meetings and site visits. Position OverviewThis is a non-exempt, temporary position. All overtime hours are paid at a time-and-a-half hourly rate. SalaryThe pay rate for this position is $31.50 an hour for interns awarded a bachelor's degree prior to the start of the internship.Monthly Way We Work stipend to assist with remote work and transit expenses. QualificationsMinimum QualificationsYou must possess a completed bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering (with an emphasis in Structures or Architectural Engineering) prior to the start of the internship. Transcripts must show completed courses in: Structural AnalysisMechanics of MaterialsConcreteSteel or Wood Design Additional InformationWork Schedule40-hour work schedule, Monday through Friday Interns work Monday-Thursday in our Orange County Irvine office. Interns have the option to work remotely on Fridays from home. Application ProcessIf you are interested in this position, please apply on our careers page. Resumes sent elsewhere will not be considered.Please provide transcripts for all undergraduate and graduate courses as well as a cover letter. In your cover letter (PDF) please respond to the following prompts:Why have you decided to pursue Structural Engineering?Should you be selected, what are your goals & interests for this internship?Physical Demands and Work EnvironmentDuties are performed in a normal office environment while sitting at a desk or computer table.Duties require the ability to actively engage with a computer for several hours per day.May occasionally need to lift items up to 15 lbs.Duties require in-person attendance, Monday through Friday, during our business hours of 8 AM to 5 PM at our office in Orange County Irvine for the training period. Following a satisfactory training period, a hybrid schedule of 4 days per week Monday through Thursday in the office, and Fridays from home may be accommodated.Our EmployeesOur employees are valued and empowered, collaborative and team oriented, innovative in their approach and passionate about their work. They are reliable, trustworthy and open with a high level of integrity. They value diversity, are inclusive and are committed to critically thinking through problems and finding solutions. Our OfficesOur Greater Los Angeles Structural office has two locations at the Bloc in Downtown Los Angeles and at the Irvine Towers in Irvine. A warm and friendly environment, we are dedicated to growing with our employees and allowing people to pursue their passions. KPFF Consulting Engineers participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.KPFF Consulting Engineers is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, ethnicity, national origin, religion, marital status, sex/gender (including sexual orientation or gender identity), pregnancy, veteran status, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, or any other protected basis.

jobs.title: US Manufacturing Internship Program - Garland, Texas at The Kraft Heinz Company
jobs.description: Employer: The Kraft Heinz Company Expires: 10/03/2026 Job DescriptionThe Kraft Heinz US Manufacturing Internship Program is designed to grow the future supply chain manufacturing leaders of our company. Over 10 weeks, interns gain hands-on exposure to end-to-end supply chain execution, collaborate across plant teams and business partners, own their growth, and deliver meaningful results that improve how we make and deliver food and beverage at scale. The internship will be project based in nature supporting our manufacturing functions based in a manufacturing facility. Program Location - Garland, TexasThis opportunity is available at the following manufacturing locations:Garland, Texas (This plant supports our Snackables portfolio)Our Interns will be provided with a one-time housing stipend. What’s on the Menu for the Manufacturing Internship Program? The Kraft Heinz Manufacturing Internship Program is a 10-week Manufacturing plant based leadership development program allowing our interns to own manufacturing projects, develop and practice key leadership skills, and support critical work rooted in driving supply chain excellence through a manufacturing intern experience. The 10-week Manufacturing Internship program includes: One week of immersive plant onboarding to learn about our business and prepare important skills for a successful summer projectTraining on the Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS), the standard of supply chain excellence for Kraft Heinz globallyEight weeks dedicated to a project exploring unlocking creative solutions and exploring new opportunities in your manufacturing facility.One week of final presentations and celebrations with our executive leadership team and intern peersWeekly sessions to deep dive into our values, grow as leaders, and develop impactful skills for early career success. Based on performance, interns will have an opportunity to return to Kraft Heinz in the 2028 Internship or our 18-month Global Manufacturing Trainee Programs. Throughout the program, Interns can also expect regular opportunities to meet with our business leaders, including the VP of North America Supply Chain; mentorship from previous GMTs and Operations leadership team members; participation in critical supply chain engagements; and curated learning experiences to help with grow as leaders and as cultural ambassadors of Kraft Heinz. Our internship will run from June 7th 2027 to August 13th 2027. What Manufacturing Interns Work OnManufacturing Interns will spend their program in one of our US manufacturing facilities, partnering with plant teams to identify opportunities and deliver improvement projects that strengthen how we operate—enhancing ways of working, core processes, and supply chain performance. Interns typically own a defined project scope, collaborate cross-functionally (Operations, Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain), and share results through regular updates and an end-of-program presentation. Project work may include:Continuous improvement & standard work: process mapping, SOP updates, line balance, shift handoffs, visual managementSafety & ergonomics: hazard identification, risk reduction actions, safe work practices, ergonomic improvementsQuality & compliance: defect/rework analysis, root-cause problem solving, first-pass quality improvementsLine performance (OEE): downtime and loss analysis, bottleneck identification, changeover optimization, throughput gainsCost, waste & yield: scrap reduction, material yield improvement, loss elimination initiativesMaintenance & reliability: PM optimization, recurring downtime investigation, reliability improvement plansInventory & execution: material flow improvements, cycle count support, schedule adherence, on-time production/shipping performance We Are Looking For Candidates who...Are pursuing a Bachelors degree with anticipated graduation between December 1, 2027 and June 30, 2029Interested in growing your career in manufacturing plantsPassionate about continuous improvementCreative problem solversAmbitious and humble leadersA drive to make an impactSimplifiersResilience in changing environmentsChampions of our culture and our values The Recruitment ProcessInternship program applications are accepted through October, 2nd 2026. Step 1: Application and Games-Based AssessmentStep 2: Virtual Interviews with Business LeadersStep 3: Final Virtual Interview Day with Operations LeadershipNew Hire Rate$28 USD per Hour ($1120 USD Weekly) Our ValuesOur Manufacturing Interns are expected to live out the Kraft Heinz values as cultural champions and future leaders at the organization. At Kraft Heinz- our values are:We are consumer obsessedWe dare to do better every dayWe champion great peopleWe demand diversityWe do the right thingWe own it About UsKraft Heinz is a global food company with a delicious heritage. With iconic and emerging food and beverage brands around the world, we deliver the best taste, fun and quality to every meal table we touch. We’re on a mission to disrupt not only our own business, but the global food industry. A consumer obsession and unexpected partnerships fuel our progress as we drive innovation across every part of our company. Around the world, our people are connected by a culture of ownership, agility and endless curiosity. We also believe in being good humans, who are working to improve our company, communities, and planet. We’re proud of where we’ve been – and even more thrilled about where we’re headed – as we nourish the world and lead the future of food. Why UsWe grow our people to grow our business. We champion great people who bring ambition, curiosity, and high performance to the table as the guardians of our beloved and nostalgic brands. Good isn't good enough. We choose greatness every day by challenging the ordinary and making bold decisions. All while celebrating our wins - and our failures – as we work together to lead the future of food.Challenging the status quo takes talent. We invest in your purpose and potential by developing skills and nurturing strengths that leave a legacy on our business and a lasting impact on your career. Because great people make great companies, and we’re growing something great here at Kraft Heinz. Kraft Heinz is an Equal Opportunity Employer that prohibits discrimination or harassment of any type. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Applicants who require an accommodation to participate in the job application or hiring process should contact NATAI@kraftheinz.com. Any applicant or employee who believes s/he has a discrimination claim (including harassment or retaliation) must contact TVA’s Equal Opportunity Compliance office within 45 calendar days of the event or action s/he believes to constitute discrimination, harassment, or retaliation.Drug-Free WorkplaceAll TVA Non-Nuclear employees are covered by TVA's Federal Drug-Free Workplace Program Plan, in accordance with Executive Order 12564, Public Law 100-71 and the Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing. Information regarding the Drug Free Workplace Program can be found at www.samhsa.gov/workplace. TVA Non-Nuclear employees in Testing Designated Positions, including those performing safety-sensitive duties are also subject to random drug testing. TVA Nuclear employees are subject to random alcohol and drug tests in accordance with 10 CFR Part 26 as mandated by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
